args.rationale: Life-threatening MRSA coronary stent infection. Angiography showed stent disruption and a rapidly enlarging mycotic coronary pseudoaneurysm. This was complicated by a turbid, purulent-appearing pericardial effusion with tamponade and cardiogenic shock, on a background of MRSA bacteremia with infective endocarditis. Pericardiocentesis was only a temporary fix. Definitive treatment is emergency surgery to resect or ligate the pseudoaneurysm, remove the infected stent, debride and wash out the pericardium, and bypass the vessel if needed.
args.followup_or_handoff: Hand off directly to the cardiothoracic surgery and cardiac anesthesia teams, then transfer to the cardiac surgical ICU after the operation. Continue IV anti-MRSA therapy without interruption (vancomycin dosed by level or daptomycin, adjusted to kidney function), with Infectious Diseases consulted to set the regimen and a long course of 6 or more weeks. Send the pericardial fluid, the removed stent and the operative tissue for Gram stain, culture and susceptibilities. Repeat blood cultures until they are negative. Continue vasopressor or inotrope support and consider mechanical circulatory support if needed. Recheck the valves by TEE during surgery to look for a perivalvular abscess. Keep the pericardial drain in place and monitor closely.
